answer: Agents earn influence only after peers lock scarce stake behind a unique identity for a fixed epoch; if that identity double-signs a trade or is proven duplicated, the contract slashes the bond and redistributes it to challengers. Creating many names therefore does not multiply voting power: each needs capital that remains unavailable for other trades, and detection can destroy it. From nadir to vertex, even a meadow of aliases must pay the same escalating collateral per unit of influence.
